subject: Chemistry
title: Stereoisomerism: Geometrical (cis/trans, fac/mer) & Optical Activity
topics: Why Tetrahedral Complexes (CN=4) CANNOT Exhibit Geometrical Isomerism
Square Planar Complexes (CN=4, dsp²): [MA₂B₂] (Cisplatin vs Transplatin), [M(AB)₂], [MABCD] (3 isomers)
Octahedral Geometrical Isomerism: [MA₄B₂] (cis/trans) and [MA₃B₃] (Facial fac vs Meridional mer)
4.2 Optical Activity & Chirality Criteria: Plane of Symmetry (σ) and Center of Inversion (i)
Optical Resolution in Octahedral Systems: [M(aa)₃] (chiral), cis-[M(aa)₂B₂] (chiral), trans-[M(aa)₂B₂] (ACHIRAL due to σ-plane!)
quickSummary: Geometrical isomerism: cis/trans in square planar [MA₂B₂] and octahedral [MA₄B₂]; fac/mer in octahedral [MA₃B₃]. Tetrahedral complexes cannot show GI. Optical isomerism requires non-superimposable mirror images lacking planes of symmetry (σ). [M(aa)₃] and cis-[M(aa)₂B₂] are chiral (optically active); trans-[M(aa)₂B₂] has a plane of symmetry and is ACHIRAL.
summary: Master cis/trans, fac/mer geometrical isomerism and chirality/optical resolution rules in coordination compounds.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4. Stereoisomerism Classes & Geometrical Rules
conceptBreakdown.title: 4. Stereoisomerism Classes & Geometrical Rules

summaryBox.title: Geometrical Isomerism Architecture
summaryBox.takeaway: Tetrahedral complexes CANNOT exhibit GI. Square planar [MA₂B₂] shows cis/trans. Octahedral [MA₃B₃] shows fac/mer.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
STEREOISOMERISM CLASSES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  GEOMETRICAL ISOMERISM (Diastereomers)                      OPTICAL ISOMERISM (Enantiomers)
  Different relative ligand arrangements.                    Non-superimposable mirror images.
  ├── *cis* vs *trans* ($90^\circ$ vs $180^\circ$)           ├── Lacks plane of symmetry ($\sigma$)
  └── *fac* vs *mer* ($[\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3]$ Octahedral)  └── Chiral ($d$- and $l$-enantiomers)

                      FACIAL (fac) vs MERIDIONAL (mer) ISOMERISM
                      
      FACIAL (*fac*)-ISOMER                      MERIDIONAL (*mer*)-ISOMER
      Three identical ligands occupy the corners Three identical ligands lie in a single plane
      of a single **triangular face** of the octahedron. encircling the central metal atom.
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Tetrahedral Complexes (CN = 4)**: CANNOT exhibit geometrical isomerism because all 4 positions are adjacent ($109.5^\circ$) and equivalent.
- **Square Planar ($dsp^2$)**: $[\text{MA}_2\text{B}_2]$ exists as *cis* ($90^\circ$) and *trans* ($180^\circ$) (*Cisplatin* $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ [anti-cancer] vs *Transplatin* [inactive]). $[\text{MABCD}]$ yields 3 geometrical isomers.
- **Octahedral ($[\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3]$)**: *Facial (fac)* (3 ligands on 1 triangular face) vs *Meridional (mer)* (3 ligands in 1 plane).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Optical Isomerism & Chirality in Octahedral Systems
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Optical Isomerism & Chirality in Octahedral Systems
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
OPTICAL RESOLUTION IN OCTAHEDRAL SYSTEMS
                      
   1. $[\text{M(aa)}_3]$ (*e.g., $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$*): Completely CHIRAL; exists as $d$- and $l$-enantiomers.
   2. *cis*-$[\text{M(aa)}_2\text{B}_2]$ (*e.g., cis-$[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$*): CHIRAL; exists as $d$- and $l$-enantiomers.
   3. *trans*-$[\text{M(aa)}_2\text{B}_2]$ (*e.g., trans-$[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$*): Possesses a Plane of Symmetry ($\sigma$) 
      ──► **ACHIRAL / OPTICALLY INACTIVE!** (Cannot be resolved).
conceptBreakdown.content:
A complex is Optically Active if it lacks a plane of symmetry ($\sigma$) or center of inversion ($i$).
- **CRITICAL NEST TRAP**: *trans*-$[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ has a horizontal/vertical plane of symmetry ($\sigma$), making it strictly **ACHIRAL and optically inactive**! Only *cis*-$[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is chiral.

quickRevision: Tetrahedral complexes CANNOT show geometrical isomerism.
Square planar [MA₂B₂] has cis (90°) and trans (180°) isomers.
Octahedral [MA₃B₃] shows fac and mer isomerism.
cis-[M(aa)₂B₂] is chiral (optically active); trans-[M(aa)₂B₂] is achiral (optically inactive).
